_about: Labelled probes for the retrieval measurement. Every query is written to share few or
no words with its target, so a result cannot come from string matching and the number
says something about semantic retrieval. Roughly half the set is Russian, matching the
Decoys make ranking mean something: with a handful of memories an unfloored top-k
returns the target for any query at all.
Changed facts appear twice on purpose. 'where do I live now' forbids the old memory and
'where did I live before' expects it -- the same memory, wanted by one question and not
the other. That is why the metric measures which of them ranks first, not which came back.
Unanswerable probes have no expected memory: the corpus does not hold the answer and the
right behaviour is silence. They are what a relevance floor is measured against, because
recall cannot see a floor -- a system that answers everything scores perfect recall.
Which probes are sealed is decided by hashing the probe id, not by choosing: see
morgan_brain/eval/retrieval.py::probe_split. A threshold is fitted on the fit half and
reported on the sealed half, so the number that judges it was never used to build it.
